newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Alliance Pipe not ruling out NOVA deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Alliance Pipe not ruling out NOVA deal.

text.p: Backers of Canada's proposed Alliance Pipeline, which would move natural gas 3,000 km to Chicago from northern Canada, have not ruled out striking a deal with NOVA Corp that would see the project shelved, an Alliance official said on Tuesday.

However, short of the project being built as envisioned, a more likely scenario would be Alliance and NOVA coming to an agreement on sharing transportation of gas from northern Alberta and British Columbia, Alliance vice-president Jack Crawford said in an interview.

"I don't see much potential for the kind of a deal that would see Alliance canceled," Crawford said. "But I do see the potential for the kind of a deal that would be to the benefit of both NOVA and Alliance."

Alliance, a consortium of 18 energy firms including Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, IPL Energy Inc and Alberta Energy Co Ltd, currently has the C$3.6 billion project before U.S. regulators and is preparing its Canadian regulatory submission.

Crawford said that because Alliance was designed to extend from the wellhead to the city gate, chances of mirroring a toll struck between PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd and NOVA pipeline unit Nova Gas Transmission -- which effectively killed PanCanadian's planned competing pipeline -- were slim.
However, he would not rule out the possibility.
PanCanadian's Palliser line would have shipped gas from north of Calgary to just beyond the Alberta-Saskatchewan border at Empress, where the TransCanada PipeLines Ltd begins.
"What NOVA offered the shippers on Palliser was exactly what they had on Palliser at a very similar rate. NOVA has not got the power to offer that to the shippers on our system," Crawford said.
"Having said that, there are shippers, who otherwise would not be connected to our system, who could do that through NOVA's system."

He said he asked NGTL president Bruce Simpson 18 months ago what rate a shipper in northern Alberta would have to pay to move gas from the NOVA system onto Alliance and where connections could be built. "I'm still waiting for the phone to ring," he said.

Crawford said he disputed figures put forward earlier on Tuesday by NOVA chief executive Ted Newall, suggesting NOVA could build the same capacity Alliance was proposing in Alberta for C$400 million to C$500 million cheaper.
The comparison was not applicable because NOVA would move the gas to Empress, where Alliance would move it straight to the Chicago market, Crawford said.
